blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Telecom, Media & Entertainment, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Interconnect and roaming reconciliation
Wholesale settlement between operators reconciles by file exchange and dispute cycles; evidence is bilateral and contested.
Network telemetry underused
Element managers, probes and tickets feed separate systems; NOC decisions remain reactive. The estate generates petabytes that never reach a decision model.
Churn saves run on campaign calendars
Retention offers fire in monthly batches; in-quarter intent signals (support tickets, usage drops, billing disputes) do not trigger saves in the moment.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: NIS2 / sector cyber regulation obligations shape the design from the first sprint.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NIS2 / sector cyber regulation and EU AI Act. Biometric and profiling constraints shaping AI deployment. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
